chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Satan (may God curse him) said to his followers: 'When I gain mastery over the son of Adam in three things, I do not care what he does, for it will not be accepted from him: When he considers his deeds abundant, forgets his sin, and conceit enters him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions that cause Satan to reject a person's good deeds?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the triad of self-deception—excessive focus on good deeds, neglect of sins, and arrogance (al-'ajb)—as the mechanism that nullifies the spiritual value of worship. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (self-monitoring) and *tawadu* (humility), warning that internal states of the heart often outweigh external actions in divine acceptance.
